summary: Sarah McVie's public content on civic engagement centers on resident-led organizing and direct outreach. McVie encourages neighbours to form coalitions, "demand better," and press government persistently (DKxwwGbyDji), and describes ad hoc coalitions across Toronto as expert, resourceful actors tired of waiting for city response (DZXdXjXRDmN). She frames her own local work, repairing harm from development, proposing solutions, and sharing emergency preparedness, as an example of that model (DZXdXjXRDmN, DZXc9u9xRn6). As a candidate, McVie pledges a summer outreach effort asking residents what is and is not working (DX9lttgx58f), commits to a 25-ward tour starting July 27 in Beaches-East York (DbE9tz4R_CF), and states a general principle of trusting residents to shape a Toronto that works for all (Da6WyC3xVG-).

key_positions.stance: Supports resident coalitions organizing to demand better from government.
Views residents as experts with immense stakes in local decisions and advocates trusting them in city-building.
Supports direct, city-wide outreach by elected officials to hear resident needs.

key_actions.action: Pledges summer outreach to Toronto residents to hear what they need and what is or is not working.
Committed to a 25-ward tour of Toronto, beginning July 27 in Beaches-East York.
Worked with neighbours to propose solutions, demand answers, share emergency preparedness information, and hold one another accountable in response to development impacts.
Reports multi-year involvement on a local community issue tied to failed democratic institutions.
